sourceManifest.subtype: wide-leg denim shorts with extended hip overlays
sourceManifest.fit: Very wide, flared legs with substantial fullness below a fitted waistband.
sourceManifest.construction: The visible garment is a pair of very wide-leg denim shorts, shown from the front. Two continuous front leg bodies meet at the center-front rise and separate at the crotch. A curved sewn waistband carries two visible belt loops and a metal waist button. A stitched fly lies below the button. Large, matching hip overlays extend from the waistband toward the outer thighs; their diagonal finished edges expose curved, topstitched pocket openings underneath. The overlays' lower terminations are not completely distinguishable from the side construction and require review. Long descending ridges in the leg fabric are folds or pleat-like shaping, not proven additional panel seams. The legs have turned, stitched bottom hems, not visibly separate sewn-on cuffs. Pocket openings and hem stitching are recorded as open edges on the continuous bodies because separate closed pocket pieces and cuff panels cannot be established from this view.
sourceManifest.materialEvidence: Dark indigo-black fabric shows a fine diagonal twill texture, pale yarn flecks, substantial folded edges, and contrasting brown jeans-style topstitching.
uncertainties: The lower terminations and concealed attachment edges of the hip overlays are not fully resolved; their closed outlines are review proposals, not installed fabric cuts.
The fly exterior is visible, but its concealed fabric extent and underlying closure mechanism are not.
Curved pocket openings are visible beneath the hip overlays, but complete pocket-facing or pocket-bag perimeters are not; no hidden pocket pieces are invented.
The long vertical ridges may incorporate pleat shaping, but they do not provide sufficient evidence for additional cut panels.
The turned hems remain part of the main leg panels; their internal fold allowances are not visible.
Image-left and image-right identify positions in the photograph, not the wearer's anatomical sides.

sourceManifest.subtype: wide-leg denim shorts with extended hip overlays
sourceManifest.fit: Very wide, flared legs with substantial fullness below a fitted waistband.
sourceManifest.construction: The visible garment is a pair of very wide-leg denim shorts, shown from the front. Two continuous front leg bodies meet at the center-front rise and separate at the crotch. A curved sewn waistband carries two visible belt loops and a metal waist button. A stitched fly lies below the button. Large, matching hip overlays extend from the waistband toward the outer thighs; their diagonal finished edges expose curved, topstitched pocket openings underneath. The overlays' lower terminations are not completely distinguishable from the side construction and require review. Long descending ridges in the leg fabric are folds or pleat-like shaping, not proven additional panel seams. The legs have turned, stitched bottom hems, not visibly separate sewn-on cuffs. Pocket openings and hem stitching are recorded as open edges on the continuous bodies because separate closed pocket pieces and cuff panels cannot be established from this view.
sourceManifest.materialEvidence: Dark indigo-black fabric shows a fine diagonal twill texture, pale yarn flecks, substantial folded edges, and contrasting brown jeans-style topstitching.
uncertainties: The lower terminations and concealed attachment edges of the hip overlays are not fully resolved; their closed outlines are review proposals, not installed fabric cuts.
The fly exterior is visible, but its concealed fabric extent and underlying closure mechanism are not.
Curved pocket openings are visible beneath the hip overlays, but complete pocket-facing or pocket-bag perimeters are not; no hidden pocket pieces are invented.
The long vertical ridges may incorporate pleat shaping, but they do not provide sufficient evidence for additional cut panels.
The turned hems remain part of the main leg panels; their internal fold allowances are not visible.
Image-left and image-right identify positions in the photograph, not the wearer's anatomical sides.

reviewNotes: Front fly exterior: uncertain boundary retained for review, not split into fabric.
Image-left extended hip overlay: uncertain boundary retained for review, not split into fabric.
Image-right extended hip overlay: uncertain boundary retained for review, not split into fabric.
Hip overlay concealed attachment edges and lower terminations remain uncertain; their closed outlines are review proposals, not installed fabric cuts.
The redraw gives both overlays sharply defined projecting lower tips that are less clearly established in the source.
The fly's stitched outline does not prove a separate closed exterior fabric cut or reveal the underlying closure.
Pocket openings are visible, but no complete pocket bag or facing perimeter is established.
The redraw simplifies source fullness and folds into a flatter, more regular silhouette.

The redraw shows two parallel dashed hem tracks where the source records one hem-topstitch edge per leg. The existing source IDs map to the upper tracks; no extra IDs are introduced for the additional redraw linework.
The short lower fly reinforcement is not clearly reproduced; its source edge ID is retained at an estimated location with confidence below 0.8.
Additional solid side-adjacent redraw contours do not establish extra source fabric panels.
Waistband upper stitching is represented with extra closely parallel linework in the redraw; the single source upper-topstitch ID is retained without inventing another edge ID.
Turned hem allowances, hidden pocket pieces, and hidden closure parts are not inferred.
Image-left and image-right refer to image positions, not anatomical sides.
Construction outlines and seam-adjacent stitch candidates require comparison with the source.
